title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The notes are written on the back of a Bourbaki typescript (draft n° 392) about restricted adèles and the density of SL(n,K) in SL(n, adèles). That draft is strong approximation for SL_n, and Grothendieck's handwritten text uses exactly that tool. Much of the hand is illegible, so the reading below is partly conjectural.

Setting. M is a motive over a number field (or a Hodge-type object). G is its motivic or Mumford–Tate type group over Q. V is a Q-variety, most plausibly a torsor or homogeneous space under G parametrizing comparison isomorphisms or integral/rational structures on the realizations.

First paragraph. Using a lemma (probably from the preceding pages, not the typescript lemmas), 'la conj. [de Tate]' is turned into a global condition of the following type. There should exist points of V(Q̂), with Q̂ the finite adèles, such that for every prime l the l-component V_l (a point of V(Z_l)) is generic relative to Q, i.e. lies in no proper Q-subvariety. This is the familiar reformulation of the Tate conjecture as Zariski density of l-adic Galois images in the motivic group, now phrased adelically.

Second paragraph. Suppose G satisfies a condition 'at infinity', presumably the hypothesis of strong approximation: G simply connected with a non-compact factor at the real place. Then G(Q) is dense in G(Q̂). One can then move adelic points by rational ones. This produces several integral structures M^Z_{v_i} (lattices in the rational realization, attached to choices v_i) which are all commensurable.

Caveat in brackets. The choice of the v_i depends on M. For M variable, it may not be possible to choose them uniformly or canonically.

Margin. Assuming the (approximation) condition on G, the Tate conjecture is equivalent to a statement comparing the adelic lattices M^{A_f} (with A_f = ∏ Z_l) to the integral lattices M^Z_{v_i}. In other words, a commensurability / integral-structure formulation of Tate.

The last line ('La connaissance des facteurs ...') begins a thought, probably about local factors, that continues on a page not given.

Purpose. The page aims to give an adelic / integral-lattice reformulation of the Tate conjecture, with strong approximation for the motivic group as the bridge between the rational structure and the product of l-adic integral structures.
errors: Strong approximation needs G simply connected (semisimple) and non-compact at some place in S. Motivic and Mumford–Tate groups are reductive with central tori (e.g. G_m weights, CM tori), for which G(Q) is not dense in G(Q̂). The 'condition' on G is therefore very restrictive, and would at best apply to the derived group or its simply connected cover.

Because the page is largely illegible, the exact equivalence claimed in the margin cannot be verified. It is not clear the equivalence holds as stated without further hypotheses, e.g. independence in l or openness of the Galois image in G(Z_l) for almost all l.

ideas.what: Tate conjecture reformulated as existence of an adelic point whose l-components are all 'generic relative to Q' (Zariski density in the motivic group)
ideas.modern_name: Tate conjecture ⇔ Zariski density of Galois image in motivic Galois group; adelic formulation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (Motives volume, 1994, 'Propriétés conjecturales des groupes de Galois motiviques'); Deligne

ideas.what: Use of strong approximation (G(Q) dense in G(Q̂)) for the motivic group to compare rational and adelic integral structures
ideas.modern_name: strong approximation applied to motivic/Mumford–Tate groups; adelic openness of Galois image

ideas.what: Commensurable families of integral lattices M^Z_{v_i} attached to a motive, compared with M^{A_f}
ideas.modern_name: integral structures on motives / integral Tate-type statements

missed.claim: An attempted equivalence, under a strong-approximation hypothesis on G, between the Tate conjecture and a commensurability statement for adelic and integral lattices of a motive. Grothendieck notes that the choice of auxiliary data v_i depends on M and may fail to be uniform in M.
missed.quote: Moyennant la condition ... sur G, la conj. de Tate équivaut à ... des M^{A_f} ... (A_f = ∏ Z_l) M^Z_{v_i}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It anticipates the adelic viewpoint on motivic Galois images (Serre's conjectural openness in G(A_f), Larsen–Pink) and links it to integral structures. This is an early, explicit use of strong approximation in this motivic context. The illegibility prevents confirming a genuinely new statement.

deep.surprise_reason: An early (c. 1970) adelic/strong-approximation approach to the Tate conjecture via integral lattices predates Serre's adelic formulations. However, the ideas are now standard in spirit, the text is fragmentary and largely illegible, and the hypothesis on G is very restrictive.
transcription_corrections: 'la conj.' is very likely 'la conj. de Tate', as in the margin.
The margin likely reads 'Moyennant la condition d'approximation (forte?) sur G, la conj. de Tate équivaut à ...'; 'réseaux' plausibly precedes 'M^Z_{v_i} tous commensurables'.
'V(\hat{Q})' — the hat is over Q (finite adèles), with an initial struck-out symbol; 'Q̂' as in the typescript notation.
